newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong rates soar on fears of attack on HK dlr.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong rates soar on fears of attack on HK dlr.

text.p: Fears that the Hong Kong dollar could come under speculative attack drove the territory's short-term interest rates sharply higher and put pressure on the local dollar, traders and analysts said on Friday.

"People think the pressure on the TT (Hong Kong dollar vs U.S. dollar) will push the monetary authority to hike rates in order to defend the Hong Kong dollar," said a dealer at a major bank in Hong Kong.
The Hong Kong dollar was trading at HK$7.7490/7.7500 per U.S. dollar, not much weaker than Thursday's HK$7.7465/75 but perilously close to the key HK$7.75 level.

"I haven't witnessed any intervention from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority but there have been rumours that they have been in the market offering the Hong Kong dollar for U.S. dollars at HK$7.75," said a trader at a U.S. bank in Hong Kong.
The pressure on the Hong Kong dollar was much more evident in the forward market, where spreads widened sharply.
